depends_on.name: key_id
depends_on.documentation: The documents a covariate takes its positions from, chosen by that covariate's `document` (its 0-based position among these entries; T15: the edge repeats one name and is `ordered`). Each must be a `value` document -- a statement (the cell list, a worm's encounter onsets) or a standalone value (a gene list) -- whose value entries, in order, are the covariate's positions and name them. Mirrors `value_id`. (`key_labels_id` until 2026-10-05; chosen by a key's `positions_from` until 2026-10-22, data_body plan AMENDMENT 6.)

fields.name: dimensions
fields.documentation: The axes of the stored array, in array order: dimensions[k] IS array axis k (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6, Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [covariates]; the NetCDF/CF and xarray model). EXACTLY the array's axes: a length-1 axis the array has is a dimension, and there is never a dimension for an axis it does not have (a one-value fact true of every value is a CONDITION, which stays on the statement or on one body: [conditions stay on the statement]). On a value document it describes the INLINE value (with `data_body` true, each body carries the dimensions of its own array); on a data_body it describes THIS body's array. Required on a sampled_body; optional on an opaque_body, where it describes the array as its `format` presents it. What is known ALONG a dimension (its times, its labels, a control flag) is a `covariate`, and a dimension may have none, a plain index ([bare dimension]). Sparse or ragged data is ONE `row` dimension with a covariate per varying fact, the long format ([no complete]). Replaces `keys` (until 2026-10-22): a key's axis and `n` are here, its positions are a covariate.

fields.name: term
fields.documentation: What the axis is (time, channel, presentation, row, spatial position, ...). REQUIRED ([along by index]: "Why do dimensions not have terms?"; "3y"). NOT unique: a channel x channel matrix has two `channel` dimensions, so a dimension is named by its INDEX, never by its term.

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: n
fields.documentation: The axis length: the number of positions along this dimension. Every covariate along it has this extent there; a `document` covariate's document has exactly `n` entries. (The key entry's `n` until 2026-10-22.)

fields.name: chunk
fields.documentation: sampled_body ONLY (rule `dimension_chunk_sampled_only`). Positions per chunk along this dimension when the bytes are split across several files (a tiled image). Chunk k is numbered row-major over the chunk grid, from 0, and lives in file-series member `body_data_k`. Every chunk is stored at the FULL chunk shape: positions at or past `n` in an edge chunk are padding, not values. A missing member holds `fill_value` everywhere, and is not allowed when no `fill_value` is declared. Absent = this dimension is not split. (On the key entry until 2026-10-22, when a sparse body's missing member was no rows; `complete` is deleted, data_body plan AMENDMENT 6 [no complete].)

fields.name: covariates
fields.documentation: What is known about the value's positions along one or more of its `dimensions` (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6, Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [covariates]; a NetCDF/CF auxiliary coordinate): an onset time per presentation, a depth per channel, a control flag per trial. Each entry is the AMENDMENT 3 entry -- {variable, unit, source_unit, approximate} plus EXACTLY ONE value form (`origin`+`spacing`, `quantity`, `count`, `term`, `text`, `logical`, `matrix` or `document`) -- with `along`, the 0-based indices of the dimensions it runs along, and `cyclic`. Its shape is the extents of the `along` dimensions in that order (for `matrix`, followed by the array's own shape). NEVER `along: []`: a fact true of the whole value is a `condition` ([conditions stay on the statement]). A covariate DESCRIBES positions; it is not a further measurement (a standard error is its own value at the same positions, T14). Same scope as `dimensions`: the inline value on a value document, THIS body's array on a data_body. Replaces the positions of `keys`, and `item.value.offset` / `item.value.control_item` (until 2026-10-22).

fields.name: variable
fields.documentation: What the covariate states about each position (onset time, offset time, electrode depth, control condition, gene). Registry-keyed for its value set (D9). UNIQUE within the list, and a variable appears at most once across a statement's conditions, its value's covariates and any one of its bodies' (a batch check).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: along
fields.documentation: The dimensions this covariate runs along: 0-based indices into `dimensions` (T14), NON-EMPTY and distinct, each below the number of dimensions (rule `covariate_along`). By index, not by term, because a term may repeat ([along by index]: "I'm still not sold on along referencing the name of the dimension term rather than the index"). One index for a per-position fact (an onset time per presentation, a depth per channel); several for a fact that varies over a grid (a pixel's coordinate along [row, column]), in the order the covariate's own array is laid out. Never empty: a fact true of the whole value is a `condition` ([conditions stay on the statement]).

fields.name: unit
fields.documentation: Canonical unit of `origin`/`spacing`/`quantity`/`matrix`. Angles are DEGREES, per angle.value.degrees. V_eta's canonical units are PRACTICAL SI (T14), not strict SI: grams, liters, celsius, mmHg. Absent for a `term`, `text`, `logical` or `document` covariate, and for a unitless number. A registered unit term (schemas/did_v2_term_registry.json), the canonical unit of the variable's quantity: the list is tools/canonical_units.py, read by tools/check_term_registry.py (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [units bound]).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: source_unit
fields.documentation: The unit the source gave the value in, as a term: the unit's registered term (schemas/did_v2_term_registry.json), its label as the name (did_v2_source_unit_plan.md). Blank when the source gives no unit.

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: approximate
fields.documentation: Applies to the whole covariate.

fields.name: origin
fields.documentation: Where REGULAR positions start: position k is origin + k * spacing, in `unit`. With `spacing` it is ONE value form (rule `covariate_one_value_form`), numeric, and only along exactly ONE dimension (rule `covariate_single_dimension_forms`). Its presence says the positions are regular (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6: the key's `regular` flag is deleted).

fields.name: value
fields.documentation: Canonical value.

fields.name: source_value
fields.documentation: As-recorded value.

fields.name: spacing
fields.documentation: The step between regular positions, in `unit`. Present if and only if `origin` is.

fields.name: value
fields.documentation: Canonical value.

fields.name: source_value
fields.documentation: As-recorded value.

fields.name: quantity
fields.documentation: Numeric positions in `unit`: `value` the canonical numbers and `source_value` what the source wrote, each sized by the extents of the `along` dimensions, in that order. One value form (rule `covariate_one_value_form`). (`values {values, source_values}` until 2026-10-19.)

fields.name: value
fields.documentation: Canonical values.

fields.name: source_value
fields.documentation: As-recorded values.

fields.name: count
fields.documentation: Integer positions (a trial number, a spike count per bin), sized by the extents of the `along` dimensions. No unit. One value form (rule `covariate_one_value_form`).

fields.name: term
fields.documentation: Categorical positions, sized by the extents of the `along` dimensions: each a TERM ({node, name}) or a LABEL ({name}, no node: meaningful only locally, e.g. a cluster number). One value form (rule `covariate_one_value_form`). (`labels` until 2026-10-19.)

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: text
fields.documentation: Free-text positions, one string per position, sized by the extents of the `along` dimensions. One value form (rule `covariate_one_value_form`).

fields.name: logical
fields.documentation: True / false per position, sized by the extents of the `along` dimensions: a stimulus presentation's `control condition` (XCO:0000099), true where the presentation was a control (Jess Haley, 2026-10-22 [control as covariate], did_v2_stimulus_response_model_plan.md). One value form (rule `covariate_one_value_form`). New in data_body plan AMENDMENT 6.

fields.name: matrix
fields.documentation: A whole numeric array AT EACH POSITION, in `unit` (absent for unitless numbers): its shape is the extents of the `along` dimensions followed by the array's own shape, row-major as JSON nested arrays (data_body AMENDMENT 4). The value's `dimensions` stay exactly its own axes; the array's extra axes are not dimensions ([matrix covariate], answer "B"). One value form (rule `covariate_one_value_form`).

fields.name: document
fields.documentation: Take this covariate's positions from another document instead of listing them: the 0-based position of a `key_id` entry on this document. Position k along the covariate's ONE dimension is entry k of that document's value, in its order, and that entry names it (gene k of a gene list; encounter k of an encounter-onset list). The dimension's `n` must equal the number of entries; only along exactly one dimension (rule `covariate_single_dimension_forms`). -1 (the blank) = not used: 0 is a real position. One value form (rule `covariate_one_value_form`). (`positions_from` on a key until 2026-10-22, `labels_from` until 2026-10-05; [along by index]: "Why isn't it just 'document'?")

fields.name: cyclic
fields.documentation: True: after the last position comes the first (a closed outline's vertices). Only on an `origin`+`spacing` or a `quantity` covariate along exactly ONE dimension (rule `covariate_cyclic`; Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [covariate details], 5.1a: not on `count` or `matrix`). Absent = false.

fields.name: datum_order
fields.documentation: 'C' | 'F' -- the order of the values of the array `dimensions` describes: C is row-major (last dimension fastest), F is column-major (first dimension fastest, MATLAB's native layout). Like `dimensions`, it describes the INLINE value on a value document and THIS body's array on a data body. REQUIRED on a sampled body of more than one dimension (rule `datum_order_multidimensional` on sampled_body; Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [covariate rules named] 6.3a); meaningless for one dimension or none, where it is left empty. (Declared on `sampled_body` only until 2026-10-20; it ordered `keys` until 2026-10-22, data_body plan AMENDMENT 6.)

rules.name: covariate_one_value_form
rules.statement: A covariate carries EXACTLY ONE value form: `origin` and `spacing` together (one form; either without the other is none), `quantity`, `count`, `term`, `text`, `logical`, `matrix`, or `document` (0 or more; -1 is not used). (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6; replaces `key_regular_origin_spacing` and `key_positions_one_form`.)

rules.name: covariate_along
rules.statement: A covariate's `along` is non-empty, its indices are distinct, and each is a 0-based index into `dimensions` (0 to the number of dimensions minus 1). A covariate is never `along: []`: a fact true of the whole value is a condition (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6, [conditions stay on the statement], [along by index]).

rules.name: covariate_single_dimension_forms
rules.statement: A covariate with `origin` + `spacing`, or with `document`, has exactly one index in `along`: regular positions and positions taken from another document are positions along ONE dimension (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6).

rules.name: covariate_cyclic
rules.statement: `cyclic` is true only on an `origin` + `spacing` or a `quantity` covariate whose `along` has exactly one index; never on `count`, `term`, `text`, `logical`, `matrix` or `document` (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6; Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [covariate details], 5.1a).

rules.name: dimension_chunk_sampled_only
rules.statement: `chunk` is set only on the dimensions of a sampled_body (was `key_chunk_sampled_only`).

rules.name: covariate_shape
rules.statement: A covariate's value (`quantity`, `count`, `term`, `text` or `logical`) has the extents (`n`) of its `along` dimensions, in `along` order; a `matrix` covariate has those extents followed by the array's own shape. `origin` + `spacing` give `n` positions and a `document` covariate's document has exactly `n` entries (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6; Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [covariate rules named], 6.1a).

rules.name: variable_once
rules.statement: A variable appears at most once across a statement's `conditions`, its value's `covariates`, and any one of its bodies' `covariates` and `conditions`; the batch check, with covariates in place of keys (data_body plan AMENDMENT 6; Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [covariate rules named], 6.1a; body conditions added 2026-10-22 [audit mechanical fixes 2]).
